problem: The tie-expansion mechanism added by the fix is wrong for CCM. cppEDM tie detection runs only when parameters.method == Method::Simplex (EDM_Neighbors.cc:282, local v1.15.2 copy scratchpad/ccm/cppEDM_src); CCM parameters are built with Method::CCM (API.cc:659) and reused unchanged by CCMClass colToTarget/targetToCol (CCM.cc:21-26) and by the per-sample local SimplexClass (CCM.cc:342), so ties[]/anyTies stay false and Simplex.cc:93-157 never executes in CCM; knn stays E+1. Probe fable_recheck_cdt_ccm_gwtau/ccm_tie_probe.py (logistic_maps_T256, full library, random=False): pyEDM.Simplex(lib=pred=all, Tp=0) equals a numpy tie-expanded reference to 0.0 (E=10) and 1.7e-16 (E=1), proving the reference implements cppEDM's rule, but pyEDM.CCM proc1:proc0 gives 0.258036085716451 at E=1 vs 0.449407364219300 tie-expanded (plain-stable 0.016209343992146) and 0.412996812927705 at E=10 vs 0.438997955936925 tie-expanded (plain 0.408547833137669); tie-free columns match both references to <=3.3e-16. So on tied columns CCM uses the first E+1 entries of std::sort by distance only (Common.cc:10-13 DistanceCompare; EDM_Neighbors.cc:226), whose order among equal distances is implementation-defined; a tie-expanded reference will NOT reproduce A[1,0], and no order-independent reference can. Rewrite: implemented_as ('more with ties' and 'whole ccmf[1,0] curve comes from the tie-expansion path' are false); the Simplex.cc trace entry should say the expansion code is gated off for CCM; deviation_from_canonical (5) should say cppEDM CCM breaks ties by sort order with no expansion; proposed_checks[0] should expect tied columns to be irreproducible (report separately, criterion on tie-free columns only) rather than 'match only with tie handling'; proposed_checks[3] caveat should say the A[1,0] curve depends on std::sort tie order; the reproducibility candidate (RNG) gains a second implementation-defined element (equal-distance ordering).

problem: Dispute ruling: the fixer is right to keep the caveat (+inf is reachable through the exact epochs_bivariate.py:328-345 arithmetic), but the record's stated sufficient condition '+inf is excluded wherever |csd| equals |Re csd| bitwise' is false, and the fixer's own p1.py evidence contradicts the sentence it is cited in. The argument bounds only Re(acc)^2 = (c*fl(1/c))^2 <= 1 and ignores Im(acc)^2; the residue |acc|^2 - 1 is fl(fl(Re^2)+fl(Im^2)) - 1 and turns positive once Im(acc)^2 >= 2^-53 (|Im csd| >~ 1.06e-8 |Re csd| when Re acc = 1, ~1.5e-8 when Re acc = 1-2^-53), whereas |csd| == |Re csd| bitwise holds up to |Im csd| ~ 1.49e-8 |Re csd|. Probe fable_recheck/pinf.py: with Re = 1.0, 0.37 and 2.9e-7 every ratio in 1.06e-8..1.6e-8 gives |csd| == |Re csd| bitwise AND a positive residue; the pipeline expression at Re=1, Im=1.2e-8 returns +inf with the bitwise test True; at ratio 1e-8 (p1.py's setup) 193,029 of 10^6 points satisfy both conditions, so most of p1.py's 216,800 positive residues occur at bitwise-equal points. The 14,280,000-point census (fx1.py rerun: 0 positive) remains valid, but the reason is that the audit data never approach the threshold: probe fable_recheck/ratio.py gives max |Im csd|/|Re csd| = 2.41e-12 (bivariate_gaussian T=1024 pair (2,1); min |Re csd| = 7.46e-7; 0 points above 1e-10). Replace the bitwise condition in the record and both notes passages with the Im(acc)^2 / ~1e-8-ratio condition and cite the measured maximum ratio; the 'wherever |csd| equals |Re csd| bitwise' phrase also appears in deviation_from_canonical and units_and_range.
